svg.title: Mount order in createApp(), and the surprises it explains
svg.desc: Nine layers, from the ShotGrid webhook mounted before the JSON parser down to the error handler mounted last. Each layer states why it must sit where it does.
svg.text: WHAT IS MOUNTED
WHY IT MUST BE HERE
1 /api/shotgrid/webhook
Mounted before express.json — the HMAC signature covers the
raw bytes, which a reparsed body no longer reproduces (5 MB).
2 express.json — 2 MB body cap
Media bytes never transit the API: they go straight to MinIO.
3 httpMetrics · GET /metrics
Guarded by METRICS_TOKEN when set; reads its own ?token= query.
4 rate limiter on /api
Keyed by signed-in account (6 000 per 15 min), IP as fallback
(5 000) — a studio behind one NAT no longer shares one budget.
5 /health and /api/health
Mounted twice on purpose: the production nginx proxies only
/api/, /socket.io/ and /review/, so /health was served by the SPA.
6 Domain routers — one file per domain, several sharing one prefix
/api/media is seven routers; multipart/* and sequence/* are declared before /:id.
departments, entity thumbnails and assignments mount on /api itself — several prefixes each.
So never router.use(authenticate) there: Express runs it for every request crossing /api.
7 /api/v1 + its own limiter
10 000 per 15 min — a polling daemon cannot starve the interface.
8 /api/docs · /api/openapi.json
Public. The spec hand-registers /health, login and projects, then
auto-describes every /api/v1 route. Other web routers are absent.
9 errorHandler
Always last: it is what turns a thrown error into the JSON envelope.
